content.title: KestrelDB Unveils Version 9 With Native Vector Search and Serverless Tier
content.text:
Kestrel Data used the opening keynote of its annual KestrelCon conference on Tuesday to announce version 9 of its KestrelDB database, adding built-in vector search, a serverless pricing tier, and a rewritten query planner the company says delivers faster analytical queries.

Chief executive Rohan Iyer told an audience of roughly 2,000 attendees that version 9 was the "largest release in the company's history" and would be generally available on 15 October, with a public preview starting immediately for existing cloud customers.

The headline feature is vector search, which allows applications to store embeddings alongside relational data and query them for similarity without a separate database. Iyer said the feature supports indexes of up to two billion vectors per table and demonstrated a query combining a vector similarity filter with a standard SQL join, returning in what the on-stage timer showed as 38 milliseconds. Kestrel said the index type is based on a graph-based approximate nearest neighbour algorithm and that customers can trade recall for speed with a single tuning parameter.

The company also introduced KestrelDB Serverless, a consumption-based tier that scales compute to zero when idle and bills per query rather than per provisioned instance. Chief product officer Lena Haugland said the tier targets development environments and applications with unpredictable traffic, and that cold starts would be "under 500 milliseconds in the majority of cases." Pricing was listed at 0.12 dollars per million read units and 0.60 dollars per million write units, with storage billed separately.

The third major change is a new query planner, which Haugland said uses cardinality estimates gathered at runtime to re-plan long-running queries mid-execution. She presented benchmark figures from Kestrel's own testing showing analytical queries on a 4-terabyte dataset running a median of 2.7 times faster than under version 8, with the largest gains on queries involving multiple large joins. The company did not publish the benchmark methodology during the keynote and said details would follow in a technical blog post.

Other announcements included support for schema changes without table locks, a new browser-based administration console, and an expanded set of connectors for streaming platforms.

A customer brought on stage during the keynote, Marcus Oyelaran, head of data platform at the online retailer Fennick & Co., said his company had been testing the vector features in a private preview since June. "We had been running a separate vector store next to KestrelDB and syncing between them, which was our single biggest source of data inconsistency," Oyelaran said. "Collapsing that into one system removed an entire class of bugs for us." He did not provide performance figures from Fennick's own deployment.

Kestrel said version 9 would be available in both its managed cloud offering and its self-hosted enterprise edition, with the serverless tier limited to the cloud offering. Existing customers on version 8 will be able to upgrade in place, the company said, though the new query planner will be disabled by default for the first release and must be enabled per database.

The company did not announce pricing changes for its existing tiers. Kestrel Data, founded in 2016, says it has more than 1,400 paying customers. The conference continues through Thursday.

notes: Medium-quality conference coverage of a fictional database release: specific features, dates, pricing and vendor benchmark claims from the keynote plus one on-stage customer quote, but all figures are vendor-supplied with no independent testing. Judge should note the useful specifics while flagging the absence of independent evaluation.
